Cross-validated scores of a fitted illume model

Source: R/ilm_cv.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_cv.Rd

Scores a model on data it was not fitted to, fold by fold: the model is refitted to each fold's training rows (ilm_cv_refit(), which for an illume fit is illume::ilm_refit()), predicts the fold's test rows, and each test row's predictive distribution is scored against its outcome. Every row is scored by a model that did not see it.

Usage

ilm_cv(
  fit,
  data,
  folds,
  rules = c("log", "crps"),
  groups = NULL,
  uncertainty = c("joint", "fixed", "latent", "none"),
  refit = "each",
  ncores = 1L,
  nsim = 1000L,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted "ilm_model".

data

The data the folds index: the rows the model is refitted to and scored on.

folds

Folds from ilm_folds() built on data.

rules

The scores, as losses (lower is better): any of "log", "crps", "brier" (binary outcomes), "pinball" (at probs), "interval" (for the central level interval), "wis" (the weighted interval score, over the central intervals at levels 1 - alpha), "squared" (about the predictive mean) and "absolute" (about the median). Each is computed from the predictive mixture. ilm_scores.ilm_pred() defines each rule and gives its source.

groups

How the random effects enter the predictions, as in ilm_predict(); NULL, the default, follows the folds (see Which unit a test row is predicted for).

uncertainty

As in ilm_predict().

refit

"each": refit the model to every fold's training rows.

ncores

Number of worker processes. The folds are shared out as workers become free; the results are the same whatever the number.

nsim

Number of parameter draws for each fold's predictions.

seed

Seed; each fold's draws use their own seed derived from it, so the results do not depend on ncores.

...

For the scores: probs, the pinball score's probabilities (default 0.1, 0.5, 0.9); level, the interval score's coverage (default 0.9); and alpha, the weighted interval score's intervals (default 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, ..., 0.9).

Value

A data frame of class "ilm_cv": one row per test row, with its fold, its row in data, for rolling folds its origin and horizon, and one column per score. A fold whose refit or prediction failed has NA scores and its error in failed. print() gives the mean of each score, by horizon for rolling folds; to compare two models' scores with standard errors that respect the folds, use ilm_compare().

Which unit a test row is predicted for

groups says how the random effects and the correlation over time enter, as in ilm_predict(). By default it follows the folds:

  • grouped folds hold out whole units, so a test row's unit is new to the training fit, and it is predicted as a new unit ("new");

  • random, blocked and rolling folds keep a unit's other rows in the training data, so it is predicted as itself ("fitted").

Random or blocked folds on a model with a correlation over time score interpolation, not forecasting: a test row sits between training rows of its own series, so its neighbours' cells inform it. ilm_cv() warns, and names rolling-origin folds, which score forecasts.

Ex-ante and ex-post

Rolling-origin folds score forecasts. A covariate whose future value would not have been known at the origin, such as the weather on the day forecast, makes the evaluation ex-post: it flatters the model. The folds record which covariates are known in advance (ilm_folds(known = )); the result says which evaluation it is.

Checks

What each check means and what to do about it, in the words it is printed with. A reference supports what was found and why; a remedy draws on it only where it says so, and anything marked as limn's own reasoning is not the source's:

  • folds and time (warn): The model has a correlation over time, and the folds are random or blocked. A test row then sits between training rows of its own series, whose cells inform it, so the scores are those of interpolation, not forecasting, and flatter the model's forecasts (limn's own reasoning). Reference: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos (2021), Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition, section 5.10. To score forecasts, use rolling-origin folds, whose training rows all come before the rows they score (the reference): ilm_folds(type = "rolling", time = , group = , initial = , horizon = ).

  • cross-validation (fail): None of the K folds could be refitted and scored. The first fold's error: (the first error) ilm_cv_refit() refits the model to each fold's training rows; for an illume fit it is illume::ilm_refit(), which repeats the model's own call. A model it cannot refit, or folds whose training rows cannot support it, leave nothing to score. Check that every fold's training rows can support the model, and fit it with a direct call to illume::ilm_model(): a fit made inside a function that passes its arguments on with ... can leave a call ilm_refit() cannot repeat.

References

Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition. OTexts. Section 5.10, "Time series cross-validation" (online edition, https://otexts.com/fpp3/toolbox.html#sec-tscv, read 27 October 2026).

See also

ilm_folds(), ilm_compare(), ilm_plot_horizon(), ilm_scores.ilm_pred() for the scoring rules, and ilm_cv_refit() for how a fit is refitted to each fold.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(site = factor(rep(1:12, each = 10)), t = rep(1:10, 12), x = rnorm(120))
d$y <- rpois(120, exp(0.5 + 0.3 * d$x + rnorm(12, 0, 0.4)[d$site]))
fit <- illume::ilm_model(y ~ x + (1 | site), data = d, family = "poisson",
                         verbose = FALSE)
folds <- ilm_folds(d, type = "grouped", group = "site", K = 4)
cv <- ilm_cv(fit, d, folds, nsim = 200)
cv
#> <ilm_cv> 120 scored rows over 4 grouped folds; refit each, groups = "new"
#> Mean scores (lower is better):
#>   log  crps 
#>  1.72 0.830 
#> For standard errors, compare models with ilm_compare().
